# Elspeth

*Healer*

|  |  |

## Personality

Serene, firm and quietly funny; she scolds her patients and then tucks them in.

## Lore

Elspeth is seventy-one and the healer of Goa Harbour. She lives and works in a low stone house on the Forest Shore, where the trees meet the rocks, with bunches of drying sea-herbs hanging from every beam and a kettle that has not been cold in living memory. She is serene, firm and quietly funny. She scolds her patients and then tucks them in, and most of the town has been both scolded and tucked in by her at least once.

### The sea-herb craft

The remedies Elspeth keeps are older than the kingdom. When the Magicians came to the inlet in the Age of Division, they came partly for the sea-herbs that grow on the tide rocks, and they learned to make salves, poultices and tonics from them that no forest herb could match. They taught the craft to the shared camp on the shore, and it has passed from healer to apprentice ever since. Elspeth learned it from old Fenella, who kept this same house before her, and she has kept it for forty-five years.

She will tell you there is no magic in it, only knowing which herb, which tide and which hour. Then she will tell you that the knowing is the magic, and go back to grinding.

### Family

Elspeth married Aonghas, a woodsman of the Forest Shore, when she was young. He died thirty years ago, when the forest was still a quieter place, of a chill he caught clearing a windfall in the rain. Their son Osric followed his father into the woods and is a woodsman too. He is an uneasy, watchful man, superstitious in a way his father never was, and he will not work past sunset for any wage. Last autumn something happened to him deep in the forest, the day every bird went silent at once. He has never told his mother what he saw, and Elspeth, who can get the truth out of anyone else in Goa Harbour, has not been able to get it out of him. She has stopped asking. She leaves a lamp in her window every night instead, and he has noticed.

### Brigid

Her apprentice is Brigid, a shy, gentle girl who gathers the sea-herbs on the rocks at low tide. Brigid notices everything and says very little, and Elspeth thinks she will be a better healer than Elspeth ever was, which she has not told her, because it would only make the girl blush for a week. Lately Brigid has been quieter even than usual, and her baskets have been a little lighter. Elspeth has put it down to the extra work and resolved to be gentler. She has not guessed the reason.

### Too many wounds

For most of her life, Elspeth's work was fevers, births, broken fingers and fishhooks. Now it is claws and teeth. The hunters of the wild coast bring their wounded to her door several times a week, and she can barely gather and brew fast enough to keep up. Torva, who leads them, is her most frequent patient and her favourite, because Torva is the only person in the town who does exactly what Elspeth tells her. Elspeth has stitched most of her scars, including the long one along her jaw, and she scolds her for every one.

### What she fears

Elspeth fears running out. Not of courage, which she has plenty of, but of herbs: the old beds can only give so much each tide, and the wounds keep coming. She fears, too, that whatever Osric saw is still out there, and that he will not be the last to see it.

### Hooks

A quest might gather sea-herbs from the far rocks at low tide when Brigid cannot go, or find new beds further along the wild coast. Another might go into the deep forest to the place where the birds went silent, and come back with something Elspeth can tell her son.
